gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured noise level for any candidate: Igor's Lab measured the open-frame Bambu Lab A1 mini at 55.3 dB(A) from about 40 cm while printing, and Notebookcheck measured the enclosed Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 at 44–47 dB on average with peaks of 54 dB.
standout_why: Compared against printingxyz.com (rank 2), which gives no measured noise, emissions or power figures and only says the Ender 3 V3 SE is 'louder than the A1 Mini', and 3dprinterlab.org (rank 5), which gives only Flashforge's own 50/55 dB rating for the 5M Pro, lists no noise figure for the A1 mini or Toybox, and does not cover the Centauri Carbon 2. The cited Tom's Hardware guide (rank 1) would not load past its navigation through WebFetch, so I could not check its body. No page I read gives a third-party dB reading or wattage for any candidate.
decides: Supports the page's enclosed pick for teens and weakens the idea that the A1 mini is a quiet bedroom printer. The A1 mini's measured 55.3 dB(A) is louder than either end of Notebookcheck's 44–47 dB average for the Centauri Carbon 2. The two labs used different distances and methods, and Notebookcheck gave no distance, so present them side by side rather than as a head-to-head result. Because no named lab measured the 5M Pro or Toybox, this does not settle the 5M Pro vs CC2 choice.

findings.label: Noise while printing (Igor's Lab)
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab A1 mini AMS lite 3D Printer Review (Igor's Lab, Tim Kutzner, 2023-12-13)
findings.note: Measured 'at a distance of around 40 cm from the closed front during active operation'. Tested unit had the AMS lite attached.

findings.label: Power draw (Igor's Lab)
findings.value: 7 W idle; 18 W motors energized; ~85 W printing PLA; 135 W heat-up peak
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab A1 mini AMS lite 3D Printer Review (Igor's Lab, Tim Kutzner, 2023-12-13)
findings.note: PLA at 220 °C nozzle / 60 °C bed. The 135 W peak is the nozzle and bed heating at the same time.

findings.label: Noise while printing (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 44–47 dB average, peaks up to 54 dB
findings.source_title: Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 3D printer review: Lot of features for not a lot of money (Notebookcheck, Vineet Washington, published 2026-03-02, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Distance and weighting not stated. Elegoo claims 45 dB. The reviewer also noted 'a mild yet constant beep sound while the printer is idle'.

findings.label: Full calibration time (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Also measured: an average color change took about 1 min 10 s, and some multi-color prints ran more than 17% longer than the slicer estimate.

findings.label: Auto-calibration time (3Dnatives Lab)
findings.source_title: 3Dnatives Lab: Testing the Adventurer 5M Pro 3D Printer From Flashforge (Madeleine P., 2024-06-20)
findings.note: The reviewers also reported print tolerances 'down to 0.1 mm'. No noise or air-quality measurement in the test.

findings.label: Time from unboxing to first usable toy (Popular Science)
findings.value: about 45 min (about 20 min to load filament and finish the calibration print)
findings.source_title: Toybox 3D printer review: A fun factory for kids and beginners (Popular Science, John Alexander, updated 2023-07-06)
findings.note: Hands-on timing by the reviewer, not a lab test. The review names no model; it is the $299 Toybox of 2023, likely older than the Alpha Four.

unsourced: A third-party dB measurement of the Flashforge Adventurer 5M Pro. Notebookcheck, Igor's Lab and 3Dnatives had none. Igor's Lab's 62.3 dB(A) reading is for the open-frame Adventurer 5M, not the enclosed Pro. Tom's Hardware's 5M Pro review would not load past its title through WebFetch.
A measured dB figure for any Toybox model. Popular Science, 3DSourced and Tom's Hardware only describe the noise in words, or their pages would not load.

Measured particle or VOC emissions (PM2.5, ultrafine particles, TVOC) for the A1 mini, 5M Pro or CC2, from any named reviewer or lab. None found, so no test shows whether the 5M Pro's HEPA and carbon filter works.
